sources.product: USGS 3DEP elevation service · regional mean slope
sources.temporal_coverage: Spatially varying acquisition dates
sources.native_spatial_support: 500 m elevation samples exported by the service from a mosaic of varying native resolution and vintage

sources.selected_file_version: Derived atlas overview; see source metadata
sources.retrieval_status: 51 elevation tile groups processed; per-request metadata in regional_slope_metadata.json
sources.interpretation_validation_status: Projection, source tile geometry, valid ranges, flat-plane and analytical slope tests verified; does not validate local grade.
sources.display_spatial_support: 500 m input samples (nominally 1.5 km 3×3 footprint); 0.05° display cells, roughly 5.6 km north–south, narrower east–west. Albers grid distances have small projection scale variation. No local grade or current condition inferred.
sources.method: Request 500 m elevation samples in NAD83 / CONUS Albers, EPSG:5070 with bilinear interpolation and a one-sample halo around each tile. Calculate Horn 3×3 horizontal gradient from metre-based vertical and horizontal units; require all nine samples valid. Angle is atan(hypot(dz/dx,dz/dy)) in degrees. GDAL average resampling across valid contributing slope values gives each 0.05° overview cell. Clip centers to bundled contiguous-state boundaries and exclude generalized mapped lake centers. This is not slope computed from the 11 km ETOPO elevation overlay.

limitations: Calendar-year 2025 land cover is separate from monthly climatology. Class 12 (perennial ice/snow) is retained even when seasonal overlays are enabled.
The underlying NLCD source has 30 m cells. This downloadable display layer is a much coarser categorical service overview, with approximately 4–7 km spacing across CONUS.

Nearest-neighbor interpolation was requested. The provider may use internal raster overviews whose generation method was not independently verified; output classes are neither validated native-pixel point samples nor area-majority classes.

A class shown at an overview cell does not establish the class at every location within that cell. Narrow wetlands, wooded strips, small water bodies, and mixed landscapes can be omitted or generalized.
Land-cover classes do not measure tree spacing, understory density, vegetation height at a specific date, soil strength, surface-water depth, or current wetness.
Wetland classes indicate vegetation associated with periodic saturation or inundation, not observed water level. Open water carries no depth, crossing, bridge, or drinking-water-quality conclusion.
Developed classes are retained as source land-cover categories; individual road and building layers are excluded.

The valid USGS CONUS source footprint is preserved, including mapped inland and coastal water beyond generalized Census land outlines. Neither outline is an exact administrative or shoreline boundary. Null cells remain source NoData; they are not favorable conditions.
Sample counts are overview grid counts, not estimates of national land-cover area. The geographic grid is not equal-area.
sources.retrieval_status: Bundled raw categorical national overview; local imagery and raw class queries are requested from the official USGS service for the viewed area
sources.data_completeness_status: 252,965 mapped coarse cells, including inland/coastal water. Source NoData retained; generalized Census outlines are reference-only.
sources.interpretation_validation_status: Existing overview checks plus verified local WMS imagery, raw class/NoData queries, time and source resolution; detailed provenance in landcover_detail_source.json

sources.product: USGS approved monthly mean discharge at stream gauges
sources.temporal_coverage: Requested November 2006–2025; each station retains its actual available years
sources.native_spatial_support: USGS monitoring stations; uneven point coverage
sources.intended_variables: Mean, median and population standard deviation of available annual November mean discharge; original annual values retained
sources.retrieval_status: 49 inventories and 1085 monthly responses downloaded and checksum audited
sources.interpretation_validation_status: Source conversion and completeness checks passed; two independent endpoint checks of daily-to-monthly aggregation passed; no ground-truth or spatial interpolation claim
limitations: Values describe monitored points only. No interpolation to ungauged channels, lakes, wetlands, or groundwater is performed.
Discharge is volume per unit time; it does not establish channel depth, local water velocity, flood extent, ice thickness, or crossing suitability.
These historical November summaries are not live conditions, forecasts, or probabilities of a particular event.
A high or low discharge at one river is not a normalized hazard rating and is not directly comparable as a risk score between rivers.
Zero mean discharge does not prove an absence of water; standing water or zero net flow can occur. Negative values can describe reversing flow and are preserved.
No drinking-water quality, potability, accessibility, treatment requirement, or reliable resupply is inferred from discharge.
Stations are unevenly distributed and are not a random sample of all streams. Some November 2025 values may still be unavailable or unapproved when retrieved.
Regulated streamgages are included. Recorded discharge can reflect reservoir releases, diversions, pumping, and other upstream operations; it is not a natural-runoff-only climatology.
Monthly means suppress day-to-day extremes; annual November variability describes variation among monthly means rather than within-month floods or drought events.

USGS decimal coordinate datums NAD83 or WGS84 are retained as reported; the national overview does not resolve their metre-scale differences. Coordinate accuracy varies by station; decimal digits do not establish metre accuracy.
Legacy WaterServices is scheduled for retirement on 2027-02-22. This snapshot remains usable, but the downloader will need migration to the modern API for subsequent updates.

sources.product: USGS approved monthly means, supplemented for the boundary months by complete approved daily means
sources.temporal_coverage: January through December, 2006–2025. 20 yearly positions per calendar month, with nulls preserved.
method: Source monthly means for November 2006–November 2025 use approved daily data and require a complete calendar month (missingData=off). January–October 2006 and December 2025 use the arithmetic mean of approved USGS daily means only when every calendar day in the month is present for the same station and discharge series. Daily-derived boundary means may retain different source rounding.
Summaries give each available year equal weight. Full coverage requires all 20 years for the same calendar month. Gaps remain null. An incomplete record is explicitly partial.

The download stores source annual monthly means in ft³/s. The app converts to m³/s with 0.028316846592, and calculates the mean, median, and population standard deviation over the available values. A single observation has no displayed SD.
sources.interpretation_limit: Station observations only. No depth, ice, flow-speed or drinking-water inference.

sources.product: NOAA GLERL Great Lakes Ice Cover Database (USNIC/CIS charts)
sources.temporal_coverage: Calendar months 2006–2025, up to 20 qualifying years; parent archive begins in 1973
limitations: Missing is never ice-free; 0% is a valid charted estimate. Surface concentration is not thickness, ice strength or current status.
Lake Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario and Lake Saint Clair; no general inland-river or nationwide water-ice layer
sources.native_spatial_support: 1024 × 1024 Mercator source grid; projection cell size 1,800 m. The source coordinate package supplies latitudes, longitudes, and lake IDs.
sources.display_spatial_support: 0.05° geographic overview; nearest source grid cell to each displayed cell center, masked by the NOAA lake IDs.
sources.method: Average valid concentration (0–100%) across available chart dates within each calendar month and year. Include a cell-year only with valid values on at least 80% of all calendar days. Equally average qualifying yearly means if at least 10 of 20 years qualify. Retain actual qualifying year counts.
sources.coverage_status: Qualifying values occur in December–April. May, June and November have some chart dates without sufficient qualifying years. July–October have no archive chart dates in this baseline.

sources.scope: Manufacturer specifications, instrumented tests and separately labeled field/driver observations; original URLs, vehicle configurations and transfer limits are in the register.

sources.product: US National Ice Center IMS daily snow and ice analyses; distributed via NSIDC (G02156)
sources.temporal_coverage: Each calendar month in 2006–2025; analysis dates, not the next-day filenames
sources.display_spatial_support: Nominal 24 km IMS grid; nearest source cell at 0.25-degree overview cell centers
sources.quantity: Frequency of snow-covered land days, as a percentage
sources.method: For each calendar month and year, divide snow days by valid snow-covered or snow-free land days. Require valid land observations on at least 80% of the calendar days and all 20 qualifying years. Average the 20 annual percentages equally. Water, ice and unknown flags do not count as snow-free land.
limitations: Values are frequencies, not snow depth, snow-water equivalent, snowpack strength, snowfall totals or current conditions. Null and valid 0% remain distinct.
Source and coverage information are in the snow data and compressed acquisition register.
